newsitem.title: UK: Arnault resigns from Guinness in merger war.
newsitem.headline: Arnault resigns from Guinness in merger war.

text.p: Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods group LVMH, said on Monday he was resigning from Guinness Plc over his objections to the drinks group's merger with Grand Metropolitan Plc.
Arnault said he had tendered his resignation so that he could focus on promoting his alternative proposal for merging the drinks interests of all three groups.

He said he had decided to resign "in the face of the opposition of the board of Guinness" to his proposals. The statement added that Arnault believed his own plan for a three-way merger of the wines and spirits businesses of Guinness, GrandMet and LVMH plus a demerger of their food and brewing units offered "significantly greater value creation for all shareholders."
The LVMH chairman detailed his plans to Guinness and GrandMet last week and was disappointed by the "speed and negativity" of the initial reaction to it, said a spokesman for Arnault's camp.

The two British groups announced their merger plans in May, triggering fierce opposition from LVMH, which is the biggest single shareholder in both groups, holding 14.2 percent of Guinness and 6.4 percent of GrandMet.
If Arnault's plan were adopted, analysts say it could make LVMH a leading shareholder in a new group, with a 35 percent stake.
Guinness later said in reaction on Monday that it was not surprised by the resignation of Arnault from its board.

"We can confirm that we have received M. Arnault's resignation this afternoon," a Guinness spokesman said. "Clearly this was not surprising since he has recently adopted a different view to the rest of the board on the future strategy of the company."
The spokesman said the Guinness board would meet for a routine meeting later this week when Arnault's resignation would be accepted. He has been a member of the board since March 1989.
